risk_if_not_implemented: Without Post-Incident Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) Validation, compromised or degraded Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) may be returned to service without confirming they are secure, compliant and functional, allowing the same incident to persist or recur. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), Delayed Containment / Increased Incident Impact (R-IR-2), Incident Persistence / Recurrence (R-IR-3), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to incorporate lessons learned from analyzing and resolving cybersecurity and data protection incidents to reduce the likelihood or impact of future incidents.
compensating_control_1.justification: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned (IRO-14) compensates for the absence of Post-Incident Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) Validation (IRO-26) by analyzing the root cause of the incident and capturing lessons learned, which surfaces residual weaknesses in affected TAAS before they are relied upon again. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Control Validation Testing (CVT)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to formally assess the security, compliance and resilience controls in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting expected requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification: Control Validation Testing (CVT) (IAO-04) compensates for the absence of Post-Incident Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) Validation (IRO-26) by executing Control Validation Testing (CVT) against affected TAAS, which independently confirms that required controls function as intended following remediation. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
